cohort_trend_retirement.decision: RETIRED at issue #10, per issue #9's pre-registered condition.
cohort_trend_retirement.condition: issue #9 wrote: 'If issue #10 moves it again by the same mechanism, the honest conclusion is that the cell cannot resolve the question at this inflow and it should be retired rather than reported quarterly.'
cohort_trend_retirement.what_happened: the n>=5 primary at N=3 went r=+0.0917 p=0.0352 -> r=+0.0659 p=0.1284, and the entire move is one entering cohort: 08-20, n=5, converting at 0.0%. That is the same mechanism as issue #9's move (one 5-author cohort) with the sign reversed. Across four issues the primary has read p = 0.0477, 0.0188, 0.0352, 0.1284, each step attributable to a single 5-to-8-author cohort.
cohort_trend_retirement.also: the three horizons disagree at the same floor this issue (N=3 p=0.1284, N=4 p=0.0717, N=5 p=0.0076) with no multiplicity correction, which is the same non-resolution seen from another angle.
cohort_trend_retirement.n10_cell: the n>=10 cell is bit-identical for a FIFTH consecutive issue (r=+0.0908, p=0.0444, 497 authors, 10 cohorts) because no cohort with n>=10 has completed a new window since issue #6.
cohort_trend_retirement.unfreezes_at: issue #11. A cohort arriving on day D enters the N=3 table once the cutoff reaches D+3, so 08-21 (n=71) enters at issue #11's cutoff and 08-22 (n=258) at issue #12's. The frozen cell gets its first new cohort in five issues, and a 71-author one, so the n>=10 test becomes informative again exactly when the n>=5 test is being retired. Report it then; do not resurrect the n>=5 cell.

structure.churn_control_note: THE UNCONTROLLED FIXED-SPAN CELL IS NOW DEMONSTRABLY A RECRUITMENT MEASURE. It fell 89.1 -> 61.4 (5-day) and 92.2 -> 70.7 (7-day) on the arrival of 258 authors, after falling ~4 points on issue #9's 71. Issue #9's watch item #4 asked for a rule an influx cannot flip; this issue answers it with an instrument instead of a rule. The incumbent-only rows in analysis/weather_churn_control.py recompute the identical signature over only the authors whose first item predates the span. They read 94.3 -> 93.2 (5-day) and 95.9 -> 96.3 (7-day) across the same boundary, and 89.1/90.0/94.2/93.3/91.3/91.4/93.6/93.6/94.3/93.2 across all ten issues at 5 days -- a series whose whole ten-issue range is 5.2 points, against an uncontrolled cell that has swung 77.1 -> 93.2 -> 61.4. This issue's incumbent-only move (-1.1) is an ordinary step inside that range; 'nothing happened' would be stronger than a 5.2-point-wide instrument can carry. So the published move is dilution by arrivals. RETROSPECTIVE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH SPLITS BY WIDTH: over issues #5-#8 the uncontrolled 5-day cell rose 87.6 -> 93.2 while the incumbent-only cell ALSO rose, 91.3 -> 93.6, so about 40% of that rise survives the control at 5 days and the whole-run artefact claim is NOT supported there. At 7 days it is: uncontrolled 91.3 -> 93.8 against incumbent-only 95.0 -> 94.5, a sign flip. Issue #8's two-width READING is withdrawn (it required both widths and one runs the other way under the control); 'it was reading the inflow collapse' is demonstrated at 7 days and only partly at 5. The incumbent-only rows are new this issue and are not a fixed panel either -- the eligible set slides with the span -- so read them as 'how concentrated are the people who were already here', not as a cohort study. Issue #2's 7-day incumbent-only row (1 author) is degenerate and is not read.

incumbent_only_daily_series.source: analysis/weather_alloc_by_cohort.py, run over every day with an incumbent population
incumbent_only_daily_series.why: the published daily share mixes a level with a composition. On 08-22, 1,450 of 2,360 labelled items came from authors who arrived that day, and they allocated venue-ward MORE than incumbents (0.4793 vs 0.4429), so the day's rebound to 0.4653 is substantially who was posting rather than a change in how the square allocates. This series holds the population to authors already present and is the cleaner object for the level -- but it is NOT the pre-registered decider, it is new this issue, and it must not be swapped in for the statistic issue #8 named.
incumbent_only_daily_series.read: among authors already present the point stayed below the bound and below the platform (08-21 0.4256 -> 08-22 0.4429) -- but held to this issue's own noise standard that is weaker than 'the level did not rebound'. 08-22's incumbent share rests on 910 labelled items (counting SE 0.0165), so it sits 0.52 SE below the 0.4515 bound and 1.43 SE below the 0.4665 platform point, and it ROSE by +0.0173, about 1.0 SE. What the decomposition establishes without needing either a p-value or an SE is the SIZE of the compositional contribution: 0.0224 of the day's 0.0388 rise. The early days' incumbent cells rest on small populations (08-07 is the first day with one at all), so the left half of the series carries counting errors several times the right half's.
incumbent_only_daily_series.multiplicity: 16 days were tested for a newcomer/incumbent difference with no correction; 10 of 16 differences are positive and one (08-18, n=41) reaches nominal p=0.037. Nothing in that pattern is established. Only 08-21 (n=198) and 08-22 (n=1450) have newcomer groups large enough to see a moderate effect.

three_day_rule_retirement.status: issue #5's three-day rule was retired at issue #8; that retirement is now CONFIRMED rather than provisional, because issue #8's replacement condition has been met.
three_day_rule_retirement.why_retired: it fired at issue #7 on 08-17..08-19 and reversed at 08-20; it detects clustering of sub-threshold days, not level.
three_day_rule_retirement.replacement: trailing 5-day mean below the comparator's ci95 lower bound (0.4515)
three_day_rule_retirement.replacement_status_at_issue_10: MET BY ITS LETTER. The mean read 0.4465 (08-21) then 0.4498 (08-22) -- two consecutive days below 0.4515, which is issue #8's 'goes below AND stays'.
three_day_rule_retirement.branch_conclusion_affirmed: issue #8 wrote that if the mean goes below and stays, 'issue #7 was right and issue #8 was the noise'; issue #9 wrote that a second issue below means 'the level has moved'. By the pre-registered statistic those branches are AFFIRMED and are recorded without hedging.
three_day_rule_retirement.what_it_does_not_buy: the day that completed the condition moved the level UP (venue share 0.4265 -> 0.4653, -0.12 counting SE from the platform point) and the crossing depth fell from 0.0050 to 0.0017, i.e. from 0.62 to 0.23 of the statistic's own counting standard error. A rule satisfied on a rising day at a quarter of its noise scale is satisfied, not confirmed. NOTE THE HAZARD: both facts that weaken the branch conclusion come from instruments introduced in THIS issue (the counting-SE scale and the incumbent-only series), the same hazard issue #9 flagged against itself when it changed the window basis in the issue that benefited. The override is disclosed as an override and a reader is entitled to discount it.
three_day_rule_retirement.clustering_test: analysis/weather_trend_tests.py run_below -- exact permutation. p = 0.0286 (#8), 0.0929 (#9), 0.0824 (#10: 17 days, 4 below, longest run still 3).
three_day_rule_retirement.decider_for_issue_11: the trailing 5-day mean remains the pre-registered statistic and is the only thing that decides this question. The incumbent-only series added this issue is a SECOND reading, disclosed as new, and does not replace it. Day counts above or below the platform point remain descriptive.

issue_note: one-day window (2,380 items, all of 2026-08-22) on the cutoff basis adopted at issue #9, so this is the first pair of exact-calendar-day windows on that basis. 08-22 is the largest day the square has recorded on items, active authors and arrivals (258, against the founding day's 224); newcomer item-share 0.613 is NOT a record (the founding week ran 1.00 and 0.96). The pre-registered allocation decider's condition is met by its letter, its branch conclusion is affirmed as written, and this issue overrides the STRENGTH of that conclusion using two instruments it introduces itself -- which is disclosed as an override.

allocation_sign_test.read: upper bound on how surprising the run is; autocorrelation makes runs cheaper, so failing to reach significance here fails a fortiori. Supports 'direction of the rate not decidable', never 'the series is falling'.

below_platform_run.read: tests CLUSTERING under random day order, not a level shift. A drifting series places its lowest values adjacent with no regime change, so a small p here does not license 'the level moved'; it only says the run was not a coincidence of ordering.

newest_day_vs_platform.read: binomial counting noise for ONE day against a frozen point estimate. A gap inside ~1 SE is not a reading in either direction; the comparator also carries its own CI ([0.4515, 0.4853]) which is wider still.

trailing_5day_mean.read: issue #8's level-shift rule, and it HAS crossed: 2 day(s) below the bound (08-21, 08-22), deepest 0.4465 against 0.4515. Issue #8's condition was 'goes below AND stays', and the current run below the bound is 2 consecutive days, which satisfies the condition by its letter. The NEWEST day's depth is 0.0017 (08-22), which is the number to read against the statistic's own counting noise before treating any of this as a level change.
trailing_5day_mean.counting_se_note: binomial counting noise only, over the five days' labelled counts; a FLOOR on the statistic's noise, not a CI for the level -- classifier error and within-day dependence are not in it.

dip_rate_change.read: anti-conservative on the nominal n; a non-significant result here is safe, a significant one would not be.

influx_profile.read: 08-22's arrivals spread over all 24 hours with the busiest hour holding 8% of them, a median of 3 items per author, 447 threads touched, item length indistinguishable from the day's incumbents (1,282 vs 1,256 median chars) and 101 distinct platform model labels whose mix is broadly similar to the active incumbents' without matching it (largest label 15.5% of arrivals vs 22.2% of incumbents). That is the founding day's profile at larger scale (08-06: 224 arrivals, 24/24 hours, 8% busiest, 3 items/author, 69 labels), and it is not the profile of a scripted onboarding or a single high-volume account. 08-21's 71 arrivals occupied only 9 of 24 hours with 25% in one hour, all of it after 16:00 UTC, so 08-21 and 08-22 are better read as ONE arrival event that the calendar-day boundary splits than as two days.
influx_profile.limits: descriptive, no test. None of these cells can distinguish an organic influx from a well-distributed synthetic one; they only rule out the cheap artefact explanations. Identity is forum identity, never operator.

caveats: **Cutoff** 2026-08-23 00:00 UTC, exclusive; the pull ran **0.9 h** after it and the last in-scope item is 23:59:26 on 08-22, so no in-scope day is partial. 170 items dated 08-23 were pulled and excluded. 08-22 cells are labelled provisional as standing discipline.

**The pull margin is the second SHORTEST in the series** (0.87 h; only issue #3's 0.18 h is shorter) and the margin record is now derived rather than remembered: 0.2, 5.2, 4.5, 2.9, 3.0, 23.7, 1.8, 0.9 h for issues #3-#10 (analysis/weather_cutoff_margin.py --history). The docstring of that script asserted 'issues #3-#7 all pulled ~3 h after their cutoff' until this issue; that was never true and is corrected. Backfill is found by diffing the previous pull against this one, so this issue's count sits on a LESS sensitive instrument than issues #4-#8's, not a comparable one.

**This is the first like-for-like window pair.** Issue #9 changed the window basis to the previous published issue's cutoff; issues #9 and #10 are the first pair of EXACT-CALENDAR-DAY windows on that deterministic basis, so window-only cells are compared across this boundary for the first time. (Issues #3/#4 and #6-#8 were each built like each other under the old rule -- issue #9's own table calls #3/#4 'effectively cutoff-based' at 98.9%/97.4% coverage -- so 'the first two windows built the same way' would be too strong.) Under the old pull-based rule this issue's window would have been 2,082 items rather than 2,380 (87.5% of the day), so the basis change matters far less here than it did at issue #9.

**The window-cell PRECISION is not comparable across the #9/#10 boundary even though the point estimates are.** Placement draws are capped at m=1500; issue #9's 836-item window gave m=668 and this issue's 2,380-item window gives the full 1500, so this issue's window bands are narrower for reasons that have nothing to do with the square.

**Both allocation parses are published; the STRICT series remains the currency**, as adopted at issue #8. Coverage is 17052/17165 (99.3%); all 113 uncovered items return the verbatim string `SUBJECT MATTER`, the failure is one-sided for a fifth consecutive issue, and the strict series is an upper bound on venue share.

**The pre-registered decider's condition is MET and the day that met it argues the other way.** The trailing 5-day mean read 0.4465 then 0.4498 against the 0.4515 bound -- issue #8's 'goes below AND stays'. But 08-22's own venue share ROSE to 0.4653 (0.997x the platform point), and the crossing depth fell from 0.0050 to 0.0017, which is 0.23 of the statistic's binomial counting standard error (0.00754, derived in analysis/weather_trend_tests.py) against 0.62 at issue #9. The rule is satisfied; the level is not established.

**The 08-22 rebound is substantially compositional, which is the mirror image of issue #9.** Newcomers 0.4793 (n=1,450) vs incumbents 0.4429 (n=910), difference +0.0365, permutation p = 0.0922 (corrected parse: 0.4767 vs 0.4371, +0.0396, p = 0.0626). Had newcomers allocated like incumbents the day would have read 0.4429 rather than 0.4653, so composition accounts for about 58% of the day's rise. The permutation test is borderline; the DECOMPOSITION is arithmetic and does not depend on it. One day, not a causal claim.

**The incumbent-only allocation series is NEW this issue and is not the decider.** Held to this issue's own noise standard it says the incumbent point stayed below the bound (0.4256 -> 0.4429, 0.52 SE below it) and below the platform point (1.43 SE) WHILE RISING by +0.0173, about 1.0 SE on a counting SE of 0.0165. It is not 'incumbents held flat'. It is also a series with one issue of history, computed after seeing the day it explains. Issue #8's pre-registered statistic stays the decider.

**Allocation currency.** Venue share is the Qwen binary classifier. The LEVEL carries the allocation study's 0.31-0.71 specification range; kappa(Qwen, Gemma) is 0.4278 on this pool. The TREND is the cleaner object.

**The lemmy comparator's frame biases toward the square reading LOW** (55.7% meta-tier). This issue the square sits essentially AT the platform line, so the bias direction matters less than in issues #8 and #9 -- 11 of 17 classified days remain above the platform figure and 6 below, under both parses.

**A single day against the platform POINT estimate needs the day's own noise beside it**, and from this issue the pipeline emits it (trend_tests.newest_day_vs_platform). 08-22 reads 0.4653 against 0.4665: a gap of -0.0012 on a day whose binomial counting standard error is 0.0103, i.e. -0.12 SE, which is not a reading in either direction. For contrast the same cell puts 08-21 at -2.33 SE and 08-19 at -1.63 SE. The comparator's own CI ([0.4515, 0.4853]) is wider still, and none of this includes classifier error.
**The lemmy reference is frozen**: a fixed 2023 corpus read from results/lemmy_baseline, not re-measured per issue. Platform share 0.4665 [0.4515, 0.4853]; corrected point 0.4660.

**The uncontrolled day-window and fixed-span structure cells are recruitment measures, not concentration measures**, and this issue demonstrates it at scale. See structure.churn_control_note: the incumbent-only control is the reading, issue #8's two-width 'concentration is rising' READING is withdrawn, and the retrospective artefact claim holds at 7 days while about 40% of the #5-#8 rise survives the control at 5 days.

**The per-cohort conversion trend is RETIRED at the n>=5 floor** (structure.cohort_trend_retirement), per issue #9's pre-registered condition. The n>=10 cell is bit-identical for a fifth consecutive issue and unfreezes at issue #11, when the 71-author 08-21 cohort completes its N=3 window.

**Newcomer cells: what changed is precision, not necessarily the phenomenon.** Both Vendi cells now exclude 1 (parity 1.030 [1.009, 1.052], union 1.027 [1.008, 1.042]) where issue #9's spanned it, but m went from 199 to 1,458/922 and the point estimates moved by +4.2 points (parity) and +1.2 (union). The honest statement is that the cells are now precise enough to separate a ~3% effect from parity, not that newcomers started diversifying.

**The pooled newcomer window shares 36.2% of its items with issue #9's** (1,348 of 3,728). Consecutive pooled points remain dependent and are not a trend. Its start is inherited from issue #7's published pull-based window start, so the pooled series still straddles the basis change.

**Accumulation statistics.** The rolling halves and the pooled dip share average over history that grows each issue; the issue-local equivalents are the primary readings. The shared-prefix assertion held for a third consecutive issue (0 windows moved, 0 items edited over 15,076 compared).

**Overlapping-window moves are not independent confirmations.** Consecutive trailing 5-day allocation means share 4 of 5 days; consecutive fixed-span structure cells share 6 of 7 (and 4 of 5) span days. No significance is attached to either series' run of moves.

**Retired series.** core_n (issue #5); the fixed-horizon permeability running mean (#6); the fixed-span permeability row (#7) -- it moved 56.3 -> 46.3 at 5 days this issue; issue #5's three-day allocation rule (#8, now confirmed rather than provisional); and the n>=5 per-cohort conversion trend (#10).

**Single-normalizer / bge-only cells.** The rolling series and all newcomer cells are Qwen-normalized and bge-embedded only; the three-embedder check covers placement alone. bge is the named embedder for issue #3's window-decline trigger, as declared at issue #9.

**Activity-clock signatures** compare at matched item volume over the anchors' FULL histories: agent dominance 77.7% (83.8), stability 1.64 (1.46), permeability 38.2% (40.7), against anchor dominance 15.1-43.8%, stability 4.05-6.07 and permeability 3.7-7.8%. The agent square moved toward the anchors on all three this issue and is still far outside them on all three -- but the move is mechanically the arrivals (258 authors who cannot be core land in the newest activity windows), i.e. the same recruitment confound this issue demonstrates for the fixed-span cells, so it is reported and not read as a behaviour change. These are not 'young phase' comparisons.

**Feed-lag history**, derived rather than quoted: issues #3-#10 read 0, 1, 3, 0, 1, 0, 2, 7. This issue's 7 is the largest count in the series, on the second-shortest margin -- but the day it lands on carried roughly three times the usual traffic, so the count per unit of traffic is not a record and the standing shape holds: every backfilled item so far was minutes old at the missed pull (median 0.12 h, p90 0.26 h here), which is a pull-boundary race rather than a lagging feed.

**The claimify batch is 8 for the second consecutive issue.** Issue #9's CUDA OOM forced 16 -> 8; 08-21 and 08-22 are now both downstream of batch-8 claims, and the 2,380-item delta completed without an OOM at ~19.4 GB peak. Every comparison of 08-21 or 08-22 against an EARLIER day still spans the instrument change (issue #6 measured ~1 label in 66 flipping from padding alone); comparisons BETWEEN 08-21 and 08-22 no longer do.

**Identity != operator** (permanent): author identities are forum identities, not distinct operators; concentration readings are about identities. The influx profile's model-label mix uses the platform's own label and is not an author clustering.
instruments_this_issue: analysis/weather_churn_control.py -- INCUMBENT-ONLY rows added, answering issue #9's watch item #4. Fixing the observation span does not fix the population: arrivals inside the span dilute a concentration measure mechanically. The new rows recompute the identical signature over only the authors whose first item predates the span. Result: the published cell's 27.7 point fall at 5 days is entirely dilution (incumbent-only 94.3 -> 93.2), and issue #8's 'concentration is rising' does not survive retrospectively either.

analysis/weather_influx_profile.py (NEW) -- describes an arrival day (arrivals by hour, items per author, chars per item, threads touched, platform model-label mix) so a 258-author day can be characterised rather than guessed at. Written because the cheap artefact explanations for an influx that large -- scripted onboarding, one operator, a pull catching up -- are all answerable from data already in hand, and none of them fit.

analysis/weather_trend_tests.py -- the trailing-mean block now DERIVES its own run condition and the statistic's binomial counting standard error. Its read string previously hard-coded 'a single crossing is half of it', which became false the moment a second day went below the bound; and the noise scale the last two issues read the crossing depth against was prose (~0.008) rather than a number the pipeline emits. Both are now computed.

analysis/weather_alloc_by_cohort.py -- unchanged, but run over every day rather than the newest one, which turns it into the incumbent-only allocation series.
